registry.notes: Added 2026-03-17: identified via STEP Bible testing during Col 2:8 exegetical review. 'Might' as a translation gloss covers strength/power terms that overlap with but are distinct from #187 strength — particularly in contexts of divine and heroic might bearing on the inner person. Primary Greek terms expected: G2479 ischus (strength/might — Eph 6:10; Rev 5:12), G2478 ischuros (strong — used of binding the strong man, Mt 12:29), G2480 ischuō (to be strong/able). Primary Hebrew terms expected: H1369 ge.vu.rah (might/heroic strength — frequently of divine might bearing on human experience), H0193 on (strength/vigour), H5797 oz (strength/might), H5800 e.zuz/iz.zuz (might/power), H0047 ab.bir (mighty), H3524 kab.bir (mighty). Note: scope carefully against #187 strength — might tends toward the external/overwhelming dimension, strength toward inner capacity. Cross-links: power (#196), strength (#187), authority (#197).
registry.description: Might is the most physically concentrated vocabulary for power in the entire corpus — the raw, muscular strength that accomplishes by force what cannot be accomplished by subtlety. The Hebrew vocabulary here is the largest term set of any registry, including horn (the image of concentrated animal power), arm, strength in its most energetic forms. God's might is the subject of some of the most exalted poetry in the Old Testament. Human might is real but derivative and limited: the mighty are humbled, but God's might is the ground of all that stands.

: make
1) to give, put, set
1a) (Qal)

1b2) to be set, be put, be made, be inflicted

1c2) to be put upon
